purpose: Two SEPARATE power scenarios for the ROM designs (Qwen3-8B reticle at 8K; DeepSeek-V4.1 ROM array at 1M and 200K), every input tagged with an evidence class and a measurement boundary. Scenario A (measured implementation) prices the multiply-accumulate at the energy OUR routed lanes report; scenario B (proposed production) prices it at a derived floating-point target lane. Every other input is identical in A and B, because nothing better than the entry below exists for either. Answers docs/ARCHITECTURE_ATLAS_FEASIBILITY_REVIEW_2026_09_27.md finding 3. Computed by tools/power_scenarios.py into results/arch/power_scenarios.json.

evidence_classes.measured-ours: reported by this repository's own routed ASAP7 sign-off (predictive 7 nm PDK, not foundry silicon)
evidence_classes.published-measured: a peer-reviewed measurement of fabricated silicon or a shipping system, transferred to our design
evidence_classes.published-spec: a published specification, vendor figure, or published design/model estimate (not a silicon measurement of the quantity)
evidence_classes.assumed: no source measures this quantity at our boundary; a stated engineering value

conservative_rule: When sources disagree or a boundary is unclear, take the value that makes the die hotter and the rate cap lower. Die cooling and stack power are each checked at their own conservative end; per-token energy counts every joule once.

w_per_mm2.boundary: whole-die heat flux a cold plate removes, A100-class package
w_per_mm2.source: configs/hardware/technology.json thermal.cooling_limit_w_per_mm2 (A100 datasheet: 400 W over 826 mm2)

scenario_A.note: The only lanes routed are BF16 x BF16 products into FP32 accumulators. Scenario A charges EVERY multiply-accumulate, whatever its weight format, at the matrix engine's reported pJ per MAC: that is what the implementation that exists would spend. ASAP7 is a 7 nm predictive PDK; no node scaling is applied.

qwen3.boundary: routed matrix-engine block (u_me) logic only: dynamic + leakage, TT corner, 0.9 ns clock, activity from the reduced Qwen3 decode step's RTL registers (1,277,952 MACs); excludes the die clock tree, operand delivery, SRAM/ROM reads

v41.boundary: routed V4.1 matrix-engine block (u_me) logic only, TT, 0.9 ns clock, activity from the reduced V4.1 step at position 7 (10,264,576 MACs over 1,088,551 cycles: a low-utilisation vehicle, so idle clock-pin power is amortised over few MACs)

scenario_B.note: A proposed lane for each weight format, derived as (multiplier) + (one FP32 add per product), because the golden fixes FP32 accumulation of exact products: a k-product tree retires k-1 FP32 adds. Arithmetic datapath only: the lane's pipeline registers and clock pins are charged by the die clock term, operand movement by operand delivery. Component energies are Jouppi et al.'s 7 nm table (published design estimates, NOT silicon measurements); no credit is taken for N6/N5 over 7 nm. Where no entry exists for a format, the next-WIDER multiplier is used (an upper bound).

fp32_add.boundary: one IEEE FP32 add at 7 nm, arithmetic only
fp32_add.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

fp32_mult.boundary: one IEEE FP32 multiply at 7 nm
fp32_mult.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

bf16_mult.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

int8_mult.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

w4a8.boundary: 4-bit weight (FP4 E2M1 / 3.5-bit grouped) x FP8 activation, FP32 accumulate: int8_mult (upper bound: a 2-4 bit mantissa product is smaller than 8x8) + fp32_add; group scale applied once per group, not per MAC
w4a8.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

fp4.boundary: as w4a8 (V4.1 FP4 weights and FP4 indexer keys against FP8/BF16 operands)
fp4.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

fp8.boundary: FP8 x FP8/BF16, FP32 accumulate: bf16_mult (upper bound for an E4M3 product) + fp32_add
fp8.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

bf16.boundary: BF16 x BF16 (and BF16 x FP8 attention), FP32 accumulate: bf16_mult + fp32_add
bf16.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

fp32.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

was.note: The 2026-09-27 Qwen production model (codex/qwen-* @5e12dc08 _prod_inputs/_rom_step) charged technology.json mac_energy_j_per_op.w4a8 = 9e-14 per MAC; that entry is per OPERATION (the V4.1 budget charges 2 ops per MAC), so the model under-charged its own input 2x, and the input itself is an interpolation between an integer (Keller) and an unmeasured FP8 rung. Replaced by 0.45 (5x).

integer_lower_bound.boundary: INTEGER 4-bit with per-vector 8-bit scale factors and 24-bit partial sums; whole 0.153 mm2 accelerator incl. 132 KB SRAM; 0.46 V, 50% non-zero inputs, leakage ESTIMATED; 2 ops per MAC
integer_lower_bound.source: Keller et al., A 17-95.6 TOPS/W Deep Learning Inference Accelerator with Per-Vector Scaled 4-bit Quantization for Transformers in 5nm, 2022 Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits, pp. 16-17, https://d1qx31qr3h6wln.cloudfront.net/publications/C02-1.PDF
integer_lower_bound.quote: Table 2: data formats 'INT4 / INT4 VSQ / INT8'; TOPS/W '91.1† (0.46V)' '95.6† (0.46V)' '39.1† (0.46V)', '† Measured with 50% non-zero input densities. Includes estimated leakage power.'; p.16: '24b partial sums are temporally accumulated in a 16-entry latch array'
integer_lower_bound.use: lower bound only: not a floating-point MAC and not our accumulation contract

gpu_tensor_measured.boundary: A100 Matrix-FP16 tensor core, control 0.37 + datapath 0.33 = 0.70 pJ/FLOP, 2 FLOP per MAC; includes the GPU's instruction/operand control plane
gpu_tensor_measured.source: Antepara, Zhao, Austin, Ding, Oliker, Wright, Williams, Benchmark-driven Models for Energy Analysis and Attribution of GPU-Accelerated Supercomputing, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, https://escholarship.org/content/qt6189368s/qt6189368s.pdf Table 3
gpu_tensor_measured.use: scenario-B sensitivity: a lane no better than a shipping tensor core

hbm_path_total.boundary: A100 HBM2e path beyond L2, regressed from board power: DRAM device + TSV + interposer + PHY + memory controller + L2-to-controller movement + control plane
hbm_path_total.source: Antepara, Zhao, Austin, Ding, Oliker, Wright, Williams, Benchmark-driven Models for Energy Analysis and Attribution of GPU-Accelerated Supercomputing, SC'25, doi:10.1145/3712285.3759815, https://escholarship.org/content/qt6189368s/qt6189368s.pdf Table 3 and Fig. 1
hbm_path_total.quote: Fig. 1 caption: 'n.b., memory controller energy is tabulated with HBM energy.'; Table 3 A100 HBM control 8.47 / datapath 4.64 / total 13.11 pJ/bit

stack_share.boundary: inside the DRAM stack: row activation 1.21 + bank-to-base-layer data movement incl. TSVs 2.24 pJ/bit (HBM2, 28 nm DRAM model after Rambus; application toggle rates); excludes the 0.3 pJ/bit interposer I/O and ECC
stack_share.source: O'Connor et al., Fine-Grained DRAM: Energy-Efficient DRAM for Extreme Bandwidth Systems, MICRO 2017, https://d1qx31qr3h6wln.cloudfront.net/publications/MICRO_2017_Fine_Grained_DRAM.pdf s2 (Fig. 2 discussion)
stack_share.quote: 'switching the capacitance on this datapath requires 2.24 pJ/bit of energy on average. In contrast, transferring the data over the I/O wires on the silicon interposer requires an additional 0.3 pJ/bit ... with the average of 1.21 pJ/bit of activation energy, each HBM2 access incurs 3.92 pJ/bit of energy (including ECC overhead)'
stack_share.stack_high_basis: O'Connor's whole 3.92 pJ/bit charged to the stack (I/O and ECC included): the stack-power check's conservative end

die_share.boundary: hbm_path_total - stack_share = 9.66 pJ/bit charged to the LOGIC DIE: memory controller, PHY, interposer I/O (both ends), ECC, on-die movement to the controller and the control plane. This assumes our controller costs what the A100's does; it is the conservative end for die cooling (the A100 figure carries a GPU control plane a fixed-schedule die may not need), and no source separates controller from PHY energy (Micron, SK hynix, Rambus, Synopsys: none publishes pJ/bit, checked 2026-09-27).
die_share.source: derived: SC'25 Table 3 minus O'Connor s2
die_share.was: 0.8 pJ/bit to the die (O'Connor Table 3 'I/O (pJ/b)* 0.80', an I/O-only boundary) and 12.31 pJ/bit to the stacks: controller and control-plane energy placed in DRAM stacks that do not dissipate it.

idle_w_per_stack.boundary: traffic-independent DRAM standby + refresh + trained PHY/controller; charged WHOLLY to the die (conservative for die cooling)

rom_read_j_per_byte.boundary: mask-ROM macro read to its output latch, N6

operand_delivery_j_per_byte.boundary: array-to-lane wire + operand register, tile-local floor

sram_j_per_byte.boundary: A100 L1 access (control 1.26 + datapath 0.33 pJ/bit), transferred to on-die SRAM

stream_fp32_op_j.boundary: one FP32 FMA-class stream-unit operation (fp32_mult + fp32_add at 7 nm); no routed stream-unit energy per element exists
stream_fp32_op_j.source: Jouppi et al., Ten Lessons From Three Generations Shaped Google's TPUv4i, ISCA 2021, Table 2 ('Energy per Operation: 45 nm [16] vs 7 nm'), doi:10.1109/ISCA52012.2021.00010

clock_j_per_mm2_per_cycle.boundary: whole-die clock distribution, fitted to GPU TDP/area/clock tables

logic.boundary: standard-cell region at operating temperature, N5-N7
logic.source: conservative production value (validation record 2026-09-27, whole-chip idle anchor: H100 bare idle 71.8 W over 814 mm2); configs/hardware/technology.json power.static_leakage_w_per_mm2.logic still carries 0.06 for the roofline study

qwen3.source: codex/qwen-coupled-schedule @5e12dc08 results/arch/qwen3_budget.json (power_production, area, dflash): the Qwen3 production power model the atlas and the review cite is NOT on main; its design point is pinned here so both scenarios price the same machine. Workload (MACs, bytes, elements) is recomputed from main's tools/arch_budget_qwen3.workload().

atlas_cross_check.basis: MAC-only: 75% of 408 W to the lanes, nothing else charged (5e12dc08 power_budget)

v41.source: main tools/arch_budget_v41.py (token_workload, distinct_experts, fill_machine) and results/arch/arch_budget_v41.json batch rows (rates)
v41.links_formula: collective bytes x 8 x (board + UCIe) x 4, as tools/arch_budget_v41.energy_per_token
